key_insight: The paper improves immersed-boundary simulations near sharp geometric singularities by forcing the near-wall solution to match the steady Stokes limit, making riblet corners tractable on much coarser grids.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the computational cost of DNS for ribbed or other sharply contoured wall geometries while preserving accuracy, which is valuable for high-fidelity wall-bounded flow design studies.
method: Embed a local steady Stokes solution near the boundary to replace the standard near-wall treatment.
Use the enhancement within a classical immersed-boundary framework for incompressible Navier-Stokes DNS.
Apply it to both a laminar one-riblet case and a turbulent channel with ribbed walls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method matches reference results in both test cases while using substantially lower computational cost.
watch_item: The approach depends on having an accurate local Stokes solution near each singularity, which may add setup effort for complex geometries.
paper_title: Handling geometric singularities efficiently with the immersed-boundary method: application to riblets
